claims.text: An ML interatomic potential trained on representative ab initio solid and liquid snapshots can reproduce ab initio-level free energies for a multicomponent high-entropy alloy.
Such an ML potential can reproduce melting temperatures and enthalpies of fusion at ab initio fidelity.
The ML workflow will cost substantially less than direct first-principles molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
The target systems are equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys represented in both solid and liquid states near melting.
Sparse, carefully selected ab initio data can adequately cover the relevant compositions, high temperatures, and both phases.
Molecular dynamics with the trained potential can calculate solid and liquid free energies while retaining vibrational entropy and electron-vibration coupling.
The proposed domain spans approximately plus or minus 10% of the expected melting range for alloys containing at least four principal elements.
Local structural descriptors in the ML potential can capture anharmonic vibrational modes and atomic interactions in both solid and molten phases.
Training on diverse ab initio snapshots will allow the model to estimate energies and forces with near-first-principles fidelity.
A fitted interatomic potential enables extensive sampling of high-temperature configurations in a multicomponent high-entropy alloy.
The approach will predict melting temperatures, fusion enthalpies, and phase diagrams within approximately 1–2% of explicit ab initio results.
The approach will provide at least a tenfold speedup over TOR-TILD for high-entropy systems.
Direct ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD are the current baseline free-energy workflows for elemental and binary systems and their extension to quaternary or quinary alloys.
Extrapolation outside the trained composition and temperature ranges may increase errors and require additional training data.
Failure to include defects, complex phase transformations, or electron-vibration-coupled states in training may degrade predictive accuracy.
Model hyperparameters and representational capacity can limit predictive performance.
The hypothesis is falsified if ML free energies or derived fusion properties differ from reference results by more than approximately 2%, or if the method identifies the wrong melting transition.

contradictions.description: The intervention says ordinary ML-potential molecular dynamics will include electron–vibration coupling, but the mechanism only describes prediction of energies and forces from structural snapshots and gives no electronic-temperature, electronic-entropy, or explicit coupling treatment.
